summary:
GAIA (Geospatial Autonomous Intelligence for Anomaly & Trend Discovery) is an online tool that provides summaries of trends, potential lagged associations, and anomaly scores from time series data across regions of the Earth system. Users can select a region of interest (e.g. Amazon/Sahel) and GAIA will automatically scan through domain-specific ‘scouts’ for the region of interest to provide live results from 2000 to 2025. The scouts perform Mann-Kendall/Sen tests for trends, Bayesian change point detection, PCMCI causal discovery with false discovery rate control, transfer entropy tests, and LSTM autoencoder reconstruction anomaly scores. 



GAIA solves the issue of extracting meaningful signals from large multivariate Earth observation datasets whilst maintaining uncertainty. The results are presented as potential explanations rather than proof of causality. The different methods are transparently presented to show how they may differ. For example, the lag 1 rainfall to evapotranspiration relationship in the Amazon passed the transfer entropy test, however the lag 5 relationship did not.

This is important as climate and hydrological analysis can be a slow, niche process. GAIA provides a replicable, transparent method for exploratory analysis to be performed by researchers, students and decision makers. For example, researchers can screen Sahel drought precursors or Amazon rainfall feedbacks in seconds before investing weeks in custom models
details:
Project Details

Overview

The GAIA project uses FastAPI and Next.js dashboard, with WebSockets.

User selects a region from the cached options (Amazon, Sahel, Arctic, Mediterranean, California) and selects a time period using the Leaflet map.

Scouts run. Atmosphere, Hydrology, Cryosphere, and Biosphere scouts are run in parallel using worker threads. Biosphere series are not curated.

Trend detection. Seasonal decomposition (period 12) is run on each variable. The deseasonalised series is then passed into an OLS and Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test with Sen slope. Bayesian Online Change Point Detection (BOCPD) is used to detect exploratory change points. Wavelet analysis is also used.

Causal discovery. Variables that have been flagged will be resampled to monthly. The data will then have climatology and linear trend removed and will be standardised. PCMCI with ParCorr is run with a lag of 1-6 months. Benjamini-Hochberg is used to control the FDR (q < 0.05).

Transfer Entropy. Links that have passed the FDR will undergo a KSG transfer entropy test. Significance is based off of 200 circular shift surrogates. This is not used as a filter, but is reported.

Anomalies. An LSTM autoencoder has been built using PyTorch. The model has been trained with a time based split, only normalisation during training and the mean + 2σ threshold. The model has 12 features and reconstruction error is calculated. Overlapping windows are used and the scores averaged for each month.

Live updates of the status of the events are displayed in the UI. The final graph, discovery table, anomaly graph and underlying data can be viewed.

The Amazon and Sahel demos were run 5 times giving the same results. 19 months were flagged by the combined model out of 312 months. However this isn’t 19 different findings as the model has been fed all 5 regions.

Advantages

Speed and ease of use. All steps from trend detection, causal discovery and anomaly detection have been placed into one interface.

Transparent. The user can see the raw data including dates, values, p-values, FDR corrected p-values, transfer entropy results and data lineage.

Honest. Disagreement between methods is highlighted. The anomaly range is clearly labelled. The demo isn’t presented as an independent benchmark.

Reproducible. The scans are deterministic. There are 195 tests in the backend and 18 in the frontend. Rehearsal scripts have been created to measure the results of the demo.

Reliable. Anything that is blocking can be cancelled. This includes variables, surrogates and batches of inference. If PyTorch or the model artefacts aren’t present the causal scans will still run. The anomaly will show as unavailable with a reason.
